# oecd-mcp

> An MCP server that connects AI assistants to the OECD's statistical database, so they answer with real, sourced OECD data instead of hallucinated numbers. It resolves plain-language questions to exact OECD SDMX series, returns each figure with its unit and a verifiable OECD Data Explorer link, and refuses honestly ("not available") when data does not exist rather than fabricating it.

Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by the OECD. Data is retrieved live from the OECD SDMX API.

## Guide

- [What is oecd-mcp?](https://oecd-mcp.com/guide/what-is-it): What the server is, the problem it solves, and who it is for.
- [Why trust it](https://oecd-mcp.com/guide/trust): The three guarantees — never invents numbers, every figure verifiable, the unit travels with the number — plus honest limits.
- [What is MCP?](https://oecd-mcp.com/guide/what-is-mcp): The Model Context Protocol, the open standard the server uses; why connecting is safe and established.
- [Connect it](https://oecd-mcp.com/guide/getting-started): How to add the remote MCP server to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Mistral Le Chat, and other clients.
- [Example questions](https://oecd-mcp.com/guide/examples): Plain-language and cross-dataset questions to ask, and how it behaves when data is absent.
- [How it works](https://oecd-mcp.com/guide/how-it-works): A non-technical walkthrough of the search, inspect, resolve, and fetch steps.

## Tools

- [Tools overview](https://oecd-mcp.com/tools/): The four tools (search_datasets, inspect_dataset, resolve_series, query_data) and the oecd://guide resource.

## Design

- [Architecture](https://oecd-mcp.com/design/architecture): How the server resolves a plain-language request to one exact SDMX series without hardcoding — availability-driven discovery, marginal-vs-joint narrowing.
- [Honest failures](https://oecd-mcp.com/design/honesty): The terminal, machine-readable failure responses that stop the assistant fabricating a number when data is absent.
